xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5018: Phone app: link to a paired machine fails with "Could not open a secure channel" on a real iPhone (TestFlight 1.0 (1))

plan.title: Phone app: link to a paired machine fails with "Could not open a secure channel" on a real iPhone (TestFlight 1.0 (1))
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: On a real iPhone, pairing with eltmon-z790 works but every later link fails with 'Could not open a secure channel'. The directory tail shows the long-running machine process did not answer the phone's offers (no ice-servers request) until a restart, and nothing logged why: RtcTransport.onSignal swallows errors and early returns, the channel listener hides closed/timeout refusals (and unexpected handshake exceptions map to 'closed'), the directory client logs no transitions, and the phone maps most error codes to one text. The phone also reuses a peer connection forever after a handshake failure on it, which makes the failure sticky.
narratives.Proposal: Add diagnostics at every layer (phone dial and secure-open logs with codes, the code in debug-build text, accept errors with mode and an 'internal' code, listener refusal logs, RtcTransport per-offer outcome and state logs, DirectoryClient transition logs, debug detail behind OVERDECK_ANYWHERE_DEBUG=1); evict the phone's peer connection after a handshake timeout or protocol failure; reproduce on the Mac rig iOS Simulator against a peer test dashboard built from this branch; fix the cause the logs identify with a regression test; document the diagnostics.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to or deploy of the Worker services/connect
- No new log-level system or logger abstraction beyond src/lib/anywhere/debug-log.ts
- No change to the Noise protocol, wire format, preamble or pairing flow
- No TestFlight or real-iPhone run; phone tests come only after the Simulator proof
- No phone UI change beyond the ' (<code>)' suffix when VITE_OVERDECK_DEBUG_ERRORS=1
- No RTC diagnostics API; GET /api/directory stays unchanged
- No log line with SDP text, ICE candidate strings, keys, tokens, pairing codes or plaintext
- No speculative fix for a cause the Simulator run did not show

autoDecisions.summary: Diagnose first: add logs on phone, listener, RtcTransport and DirectoryClient, reproduce on the iOS Simulator, then fix the cause the logs show
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's suggested steps and the operator comment both prescribe this order; the long-uptime cause cannot be proven by reading code.

autoDecisions.summary: 'Debug build' for the on-screen error code means the web bundle flag VITE_OVERDECK_DEBUG_ERRORS=1
autoDecisions.rationale: Xcode Debug/Release does not reach the Vite bundle; the only native signal (pushEnvironment) is async and iOS-only; a build flag matches VITE_OVERDECK_REQUEST_LOG.

autoDecisions.summary: Machine debug lines are gated by OVERDECK_ANYWHERE_DEBUG=1 through one helper src/lib/anywhere/debug-log.ts
autoDecisions.rationale: No log-level system exists; closed refusals happen in normal phased probing and would flood dashboard.log.

autoDecisions.summary: Per-offer, per-outcome, per-state-change RTC lines and directory transitions are always on
autoDecisions.rationale: The failure only shows in a long-running process, so a flag set afterwards would miss it; these events are rare.

autoDecisions.summary: The phone evicts its peer connections to a machine after a handshake timeout or protocol failure, not after a definitive refusal or busy
autoDecisions.rationale: 'Could not open a secure channel' is only produced after a raw channel opened, and a reused zombie connection is never evicted today, which makes the failure sticky.

autoDecisions.summary: Unexpected exceptions inside acceptChannel get the new code 'internal' instead of 'closed'
autoDecisions.rationale: Today a real handshake bug maps to 'closed', which the listener never logs.

autoDecisions.summary: The Simulator run uses a peer test dashboard built from this branch with its own HOME, not the operator's live dashboard
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's dashboard runs main; the new logs and fixes must be on the machine side of the test.

autoDecisions.summary: The Worker services/connect is not changed or deployed in this issue
autoDecisions.rationale: Keeps the change inside the repo's deploy path; if logs prove frames never reach the machine, a follow-up issue covers a Worker delivery count.

autoDecisions.summary: If the Simulator scenario does not reproduce the failure, ship the diagnostics and the eviction, post the evidence on the issue and use 'Refs PAN-5018'
autoDecisions.rationale: A speculative fix for an unobserved cause would violate the no-speculation rule; the operator still gets the logs for the next phone test.

narrative.Action: PRD .pan/drafts/pan-5018.md WI-1. Add optional dep `log` to ConnectionDeps (default console.warn with '[overdeck] ' prefix). In dialRaw log the swallowed remembered-relay failure, the direct failure and the relay failure ('link <label>: direct dial failed: <message>' / 'relay dial failed'). In secure() log 'link <label>: secure open failed over <direct|relay> (<code>): <message>' before throwing channelError. Track the route with an internal helper; the public dialRaw signature stays unchanged. Never log keys, tokens or SDP.

Given openSecureChannel rejects with ChannelOpenError('timeout'), when openLink runs, then the injected log receives a line containing 'secure open failed over direct (timeout)'
Given the existing it.each error-mapping table, when connection.test.ts runs, then every existing case still returns the same on-screen text

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. config.ts: export DEBUG_ERRORS = env.VITE_OVERDECK_DEBUG_ERRORS === '1'. connection.ts: optional dep showErrorCodes (default DEBUG_ERRORS); channelError(error, label, showCode) appends ' (<code>)' for a ChannelOpenError when showCode is true. In secure()'s catch, when the ChannelOpenError code is 'timeout' or 'protocol', delete the remembered route and call directory.dialer.close(environmentId) before throwing (decision D-5). Never evict on unknown-peer, pairing-refused, identity-refused, unsupported or busy.

Reproduce the link failure on the iOS Simulator with the new logs

expected_outputs: ACCEPTANCE.md contains a PAN-5018 section with scenario times, on-screen texts and log lines

narrative.Action: PRD WI-8 (implementation checkpoint). Build this branch; start a peer test dashboard with its own HOME/OVERDECK_HOME, PORT=3061, OVERDECK_ANYWHERE_SUPERVISOR=1, OVERDECK_ANYWHERE_DEBUG=1, launched through a symlink path that does not contain dist/dashboard/server.js; sign it in (ask the operator only to type credentials, D-8). Build the phone bundle with VITE_OVERDECK_DEBUG_ERRORS=1 and run it in a dedicated Mac rig Simulator per apps/mobile/README.md; pair via simctl openurl. Run the scenario (>=30 min uptime, 5 open/close, 3 background/foreground, one SIGSTOP 90 s directory reconnect, one cold launch), record each step's on-screen text and matching phone ([overdeck]) and machine ([anywhere]) log lines, and classify the failure with the PRD decision table. Fallback: rerun with 2 h uptime; if still not reproduced, record 'not reproduced'.

items.title: Given the scenario has run, when apps/mobile/ACCEPTANCE.md is read, then its PAN-5018 section lists each step with its time, the on-screen text and the matching phone and machine log lines
Given a step failed, when the section is read, then it names the matching decision-table row; given no step failed after the 2 h rerun, then it states 'not reproduced'
Fix the cause the Simulator run identified, with a regression test

expected_outputs: all three test files pass, including the new regression test in the file the fix touched

narrative.Action: PRD WI-9. Apply the fix named by the matched decision-table row in WI-8. Write a regression test that builds the faulty state directly and asserts the right outcome; check it fails on the pre-fix code (never git stash; comment the fix out locally or use git show HEAD~1:<file> into a scratch copy) and say so in the commit message. Rerun the WI-8 scenario on the Simulator and add the passing result to ACCEPTANCE.md. Fallback when WI-8 recorded 'not reproduced': post an issue comment on PAN-5018 with the scenario, run times and log lines, write 'Refs PAN-5018' (not 'Fixes') in the PR body, and add no speculative fix.

items.title: Given WI-8 identified a cause, when the regression test runs on the fixed code, then it passes, and the commit message states it failed before the fix

Given WI-8 recorded 'not reproduced', when this item completes, then PAN-5018 has a comment with the evidence and the PR body contains 'Refs PAN-5018' and no 'Fixes PAN-5018'

metadata.sizeJustification: One bug on one phone-to-machine link: the diagnostics must exist on both ends (apps/mobile, packages/anywhere-channel, src/lib/anywhere, src/dashboard/server) before the single Simulator reproduction can classify the cause, and the fix depends on that run. Sibling issues would split the reproduction from the logs it reads. The 7th subsystem is documentation (docs/, configuration/, .overdeck/context). 20 files, under the 25-file limit.
